questions.q: What is this course's actual goal, stated plainly in this lesson?
options: To make you able to read an existing PowerShell script, understand it, modify it safely, and run it — not write a 500-line module from scratch
To train you into a full-time professional PowerShell software developer
To replace the need for ever learning T-SQL
To teach PowerShell purely as an academic exercise with no practical application
questions.explain: This course is explicitly aimed at DBAs and admins who need to read, modify, and use scripts — not become developers.

questions.q: What is the single biggest adjustment for someone coming from bash or cmd.exe, according to this lesson?
options: PowerShell's pipeline passes real objects between commands, not plain text
PowerShell has no concept of a pipeline at all
PowerShell commands never accept any arguments
PowerShell only works inside SQL Server Management Studio
questions.explain: This object-based pipeline is the reason Chapter 2 gives objects-versus-text its own dedicated lesson.

questions.q: Why does piping real objects make a PowerShell script more reliable than an equivalent bash script parsing text output?
options: A bash script parsing text output silently depends on that text format never changing; a PowerShell script works with real properties on a real object instead
Bash scripts are always more reliable than PowerShell scripts
There is no real difference in reliability between the two approaches
PowerShell scripts cannot process any output from a command at all
questions.explain: Text-parsing breaks silently when output formatting changes; object properties don't have that fragility.

questions.q: How does this course relate to Azure Database Administrator Lesson 66's PowerShell/CLI coverage?
options: Lesson 66 gave a DBA-level overview in the moment it was needed; this course is the actual depth behind that overview
This course has no relationship to Azure Database Administrator at all
This course replaces the need for Azure Database Administrator entirely
Lesson 66 already covered everything this course teaches, making this course redundant
questions.explain: This course builds the real depth that a single overview lesson in the DBA course couldn't provide on its own.

questions.q: What does Chapter 4 specifically add, compared to Chapters 1-3?
options: It stops being generic PowerShell and becomes specifically useful for Azure and SQL — the Az module, dbatools, and a real automated script
It repeats Chapter 1's basics in more detail
It focuses exclusively on PowerShell syntax with no practical application
It has no connection to Azure or SQL Server at all
questions.explain: Chapter 4 is where the course connects back to the practical Azure/SQL work the rest of this catalog assumes.
